Stat. 12-211

In-scope processes.value: Annual premium tax computation for each foreign writing company: Schedule T premium allocation, taxable-basis adjustments, taxing-state aggregate burden, domiciliary-state mirror burden, retaliatory excess by state, GL accrual. checklist.step: Freeze the writing-company and domicile inventory for the tax year
actions: Open the current-year Annual Statement for each writing company and copy from the Jurat page: legal name, NAIC company code, FEIN, state of domicile and the states in which the company is licensed.

Ask the Regulatory Filing Specialist for the certificate of authority list by state and reconcile it to the Jurat licensed-state list; a state on either list but not the other must be resolved before any computation starts.
For any alien insurer or U.S. branch, record the state of entry (port of entry) instead of a domicile, because that is the state whose burden the retaliatory comparison mirrors.
Record any redomestication during the year, with its effective date, and note that the comparison basis changes on that date.
Write the resulting company / domicile / licensed-state grid onto the control tab of the retaliatory workbook.
checklist.done: every writing company has a confirmed domicile (or port of entry), a licensed-state list agreeing to the certificates of authority, and any redomestication is dated.

checklist.step: Pull direct premiums written by state and company from Schedule T
actions: Export Schedule T (Exhibit of Premiums Written Allocated by States and Territories) from the filed Annual Statement for each writing company, by state and by column (direct premiums written, direct premiums earned, dividends, finance and service charges).
Export the State Page (Exhibit of Premiums and Losses, statutory page 14) for the same companies so line-of-business detail is available for states that tax by line.
Confirm the Schedule T grand total agrees to the Underwriting and Investment Exhibit direct premium written total and note the difference if it does not.
Hand the extract to the Tax Analyst as a locked, dated file named schedT-<company>-<tax year>.xlsx and keep the export parameters with it.
checklist.done: a dated Schedule T and State Page extract per writing company is delivered to Tax and its grand total ties to the filed statement.

checklist.step: Build the taxable premium basis for each state
actions: Start each state row from Schedule T direct premiums written for that state and writing company.

Apply the state's own basis rules: subtract return premiums and policyholder dividends where the state allows them, add finance and service charges where the state taxes them, and exclude premium the state does not tax (for example most states exclude annuity considerations and federally-reinsured crop premium).
Split the basis by line where the state applies different rates (Alabama taxes life at a different rate from all-other business under Ala. Code 27-4A-3), pulling the line split from the State Page.
Deduct premium written on risks located outside the state or reported to a different state under the state's allocation rule, and document which allocation rule you applied.
Show every adjustment as its own labelled line so the basis walks visibly from Schedule T to taxable premium.
checklist.done: each state row shows a visible walk from Schedule T direct written premium to taxable premium, with every adjustment labelled and sourced.

checklist.step: Refresh the rate and fee tables from the current-year NAIC Retaliation Guide
actions: Download the current-year NAIC Retaliation Guide (Volume I property/casualty, Volume II life/health) from the NAIC account portal as soon as it publishes in January.

For each state in scope, transcribe into the rate table: premium tax rate by line, fire marshal or fire department tax, annual statement filing fee, certificate of authority renewal fee, examination and valuation fees, agent appointment and renewal fees, and any special assessments the guide flags as retaliatory-includable.
Record for each figure the Retaliation Guide page and the statutory cite the guide gives, so the number can be defended without re-research.
Cross-check the three largest states by premium against the state department of insurance website or a current-year tax bulletin, because the guide lags mid-year rate changes.
Date-stamp the table <state>-rates-<yyyy-mm-dd> and lock it; any later change is made as a tracked revision, never an overwrite.
checklist.done: a dated, page-referenced rate and fee table exists for every in-scope state and the three largest states are corroborated against a primary source.

checklist.step: Compute the taxing state aggregate burden — Alabama as the representative state
actions: On the Alabama tab, multiply the Alabama taxable premium by the Alabama statutory rate under Ala. Code 27-4A-3 for each line of business and sum to Alabama basic premium tax.

Add the Alabama fixed impositions the retaliatory statute treats as part of the burden: annual statement filing fee, certificate of authority renewal fee, and agent appointment and renewal fees actually incurred for Alabama.

Subtract any Alabama credit the statute allows in the burden computation (for example the Alabama office facilities and real property investment credits) and note whether the state's retaliatory rule requires the burden to be measured before or after that credit.
Total the result as Alabama aggregate burden and label each component with its statutory cite.
Repeat the same build on every other state tab using that state's own rate table.
checklist.done: every state tab shows an aggregate taxing-state burden built from labelled, cited components rather than a single blended rate.

checklist.step: Compute the domiciliary state mirror burden for the same premium
actions: On each state tab, apply the writing company's domiciliary state rates and fees to that same taxing-state taxable premium, as if a company domiciled in the taxing state were writing that business in the domiciliary state.

Include in the mirror the domiciliary state's premium tax, fire marshal tax, filing and certificate of authority fees, and agent appointment fees — matching component for component with the taxing-state burden.
Use the domiciliary rate schedule effective for the tax year, not the current year, and record the effective date beside each figure.
Where the domiciliary state grants a home-office or investment credit, apply the treatment the taxing state's statute prescribes and quote that sentence on the tab.
Total the result as domiciliary mirror burden.
checklist.done: each state tab carries a component-for-component domiciliary mirror burden using tax-year-effective domiciliary rates.

checklist.step: Classify each imposition as includable or an excluded special-purpose obligation
actions: Read the taxing state's retaliatory statute and list what it says is compared — most statutes compare taxes, licenses, fees, fines, penalties, deposit requirements and other obligations, and exclude ad valorem taxes on real or personal property and special-purpose obligations or assessments.
Tag every line on the tab INCLUDABLE or EXCLUDED and paste the statutory phrase relied on next to the tag.

Treat guaranty association assessments, second injury fund and workers compensation special assessments as excluded unless the state's own guide entry says otherwise, and document the call either way.
Send any line you cannot resolve from the statute and the guide to Regulatory Counsel with the two candidate treatments and the dollar impact.
Apply the same classification consistently on both sides of the comparison — an item excluded from the taxing-state burden must also be excluded from the mirror.
checklist.done: every imposition on both sides carries an INCLUDABLE or EXCLUDED tag with a quoted statutory basis, applied symmetrically.

checklist.step: Apply guaranty fund assessment offsets and premium tax credits
actions: Pull from the GL the guaranty association assessments paid by state and year and the unused offset carryforward balance from the prior-year workpaper.
Apply each state's offset rule — many states allow the assessment to be recovered against premium tax in equal instalments over five years at 20 percent per year beginning the year after payment.
Record the offset taken, the remaining carryforward and the expiry year on a per-state credit schedule.
Determine whether the state's retaliatory rule measures the burden before or after the offset, and place the offset on the correct side of the comparison.
Reconcile the total credits claimed on the schedule to the deferred tax credit asset carried in the GL.
checklist.done: the credit schedule shows offsets taken, carryforwards and expiries by state and reconciles to the GL credit asset.

checklist.step: Compute the retaliatory excess and take the greater of the two burdens
actions: For each state, compute retaliatory tax = domiciliary mirror burden minus taxing-state aggregate burden, floored at zero — a negative result never creates a refund.

Set total tax due to the taxing state = taxing-state basic premium tax plus the retaliatory excess, and confirm that equals the greater of the two aggregate burdens less the fixed fees billed separately.
Force the retaliatory line to zero on the company's own domiciliary state tab and add a note that a domestic insurer is not subject to retaliation.
Flag every state where the retaliatory excess moves more than 10 percent against last year and write a one-line driver (rate change, premium mix shift, domicile change) beside it.
Roll all state results into a summary tab showing basic tax, retaliatory tax and total by company and by state.
checklist.done: every state shows a floored-at-zero retaliatory excess, domestic states show zero, and year-over-year movers above 10 percent carry a written driver.

checklist.step: Bring municipal, county and fire marshal taxes into the comparison correctly
actions: List the local impositions the company actually paid by state — Kentucky local government premium tax, Louisiana and South Carolina municipal taxes, fire marshal or fire department taxes, and state surcharges.

For each, check whether the state's retaliatory statute or the NAIC Retaliation Guide entry brings local taxes into the aggregate burden; several states expressly exclude municipal taxes and Alabama preempts municipal license taxes under Ala. Code 27-4A-1.
Where local taxes are included, source the paid amounts from the local tax filings rather than the GL accrual, and reconcile the two.
Document each inclusion or exclusion decision on the state tab with the cite that drove it.
checklist.done: every local imposition is either in the burden with a paid-amount source or excluded with a cite, on both sides of each comparison.

checklist.step: Capture the licensing and appointment fees that feed the burden
actions: In NIPR Gateway run the appointment and renewal activity report for the tax year, by state and by writing company.
Total appointment fees, appointment renewal fees and any per-producer state charges paid for each state and hand the totals to the Tax Analyst.
Add the company-level fees from the state invoices: annual statement filing fee, certificate of authority renewal fee, and any examination or valuation fee billed in the year.
Reconcile the NIPR totals to the fees expensed in the GL licensing account and explain any difference before the totals are used.
checklist.done: a per-state fee total covering appointments, renewals, filing and certificate of authority fees is delivered to Tax and reconciles to the GL.

checklist.step: Tie the computed tax to the general ledger accrual
actions: Pull the premium tax expense and premium tax payable account balances by company and state from the GL trial balance.
Compare the workbook total tax by state to the accrued balance, and build a reconciling schedule for prepayments already made, prior-year true-ups and credits applied.
Post the true-up journal entry for the difference, referencing the workbook version and the state, and route it for Controller approval.
Confirm the resulting payable equals the amount that will be remitted with the return so the filing and the ledger cannot diverge.
checklist.done: the workbook total by state agrees to the GL premium tax payable after a documented reconciling schedule and an approved true-up entry.

checklist.step: Run the preparer-to-reviewer review and lock the workbook
actions: Review each state tab against a fixed checklist: correct domicile, tax-year-effective rates on both sides, symmetric includable classification, floor at zero, credits on the correct side, basis tied to Schedule T.
Re-perform from scratch the five states with the largest retaliatory balances rather than reviewing the preparer's arithmetic.
Return every question to the Tax Analyst in writing and require the answer on the tab, not by email only.
Sign the control tab with preparer name, reviewer name and date, then set the workbook to read-only as version <tax year>-FINAL.
checklist.done: the workbook is signed by a preparer and a separate reviewer, the top five states are independently re-performed, and the file is locked as FINAL.

checklist.step: Report the retaliatory result to the Controller and Financial Planning
actions: Present the summary tab to the Controller: total premium tax, total retaliatory tax, effective tax rate on direct written premium, and the year-over-year bridge.
Call out the states where a domicile change, a rate change or a premium mix shift moved the retaliatory number materially, so pricing and planning can react.
Hand FP&A the state-level forecast basis for next year's accrual rate.
Record the review date and attendees on the control tab.
checklist.done: the Controller has accepted the result and the year-over-year bridge, with the review date recorded on the workbook.

checklist.step: File the computation evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the locked workbook, the dated NAIC Retaliation Guide extracts, the Schedule T export, the NIPR fee report, the credit schedule and the sign-off page into the repository under Tax / Premium Tax / retaliatory / <tax year>.
Apply the 7-year retention label measured from the return due date so the record outlives every state assessment window.
Confirm the index makes the record searchable by writing company, NAIC company code, state and tax year.
Record the repository link on the tax calendar row for each state so a state examiner request can be answered from the calendar.
checklist.done: the complete computation package is filed, labelled for 7-year retention and retrievable by company, state and tax year.

testing.step: Build the population of company and state computations for the tax year
actions: Extract Schedule T for every writing company and list every state carrying direct premiums written, plus every state where the company holds a certificate of authority with zero premium.
Match that list to the tabs present in the locked retaliatory workbook and list any state present in one and absent from the other.
Confirm the population covers all 51 jurisdictions for each foreign-licensed company before sampling begins.
Sign the population extract with the extraction date and the workbook version tested.
testing.done: the population is reconciled tab-for-state against Schedule T, signed and dated, with any missing state already listed as an exception.

testing.step: Reconcile taxable premium and total tax to the statements and the ledger
actions: Sum workbook taxable premium by company and agree it to Schedule T direct premiums written less the documented basis adjustments.
Agree total tax by state from the summary tab to the GL premium tax payable and expense balances, using the preparer's reconciling schedule.
Test every reconciling item over the materiality threshold back to its source document, not to the schedule that asserts it.
Treat any unexplained residual above USD 500 per state as an exception rather than a rounding difference.
testing.done: workbook premium and tax reconcile to Schedule T and the GL, with every material reconciling item traced to source.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of state computations
actions: Take 100 percent of states where the retaliatory excess exceeds USD 100,000 or where the excess moved more than 25 percent year over year.
Take 20 further state rows by seeded random selection from the remainder, with a floor of 35 rows overall.
Force into the sample every state where the writing company redomesticated during the year and every alien or U.S. branch entity.
Record the seed, the population size, the stratification rule and the draw date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed, and covers every large, volatile and redomestication state row.

testing.step: Re-perform the domicile determination for each sampled company
actions: Open the filed Annual Statement Jurat page and read the state of domicile independently of the workbook.
For alien insurers and U.S. branches, confirm the port of entry from the certificate of authority rather than assuming the state of the U.S. management office.
Where a redomestication occurred, confirm the workbook split the year at the effective date and used each domicile's rates for its own period.
Treat a wrong domicile as an automatic fail — it invalidates the whole comparison for that state.
testing.done: each sampled company's domicile or port of entry is independently confirmed and any redomestication split is verified.

testing.step: Re-perform the taxing state burden from the NAIC Retaliation Guide
actions: For each sampled state, open the tax-year NAIC Retaliation Guide entry and read the premium tax rate, fire marshal tax, filing fee, certificate of authority fee and appointment fees without looking at the workbook first.
Rebuild the taxing-state aggregate burden on your own schedule using the sampled taxable premium.
Compare to the workbook figure and investigate any difference above the lower of USD 500 or 0.5 percent of that state's total tax.
Capture the guide page you relied on into the workpaper with its publication date.
Verify the sampled rates against the state department of insurance bulletin for the two states with the largest balances.
testing.done: each sampled state has an independently rebuilt taxing-state burden within threshold, with the source guide page captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the domiciliary mirror burden and the excess arithmetic
actions: Rebuild the domiciliary mirror using the domiciliary state's tax-year-effective rates applied to the same taxable premium, component for component.
Recompute retaliatory tax = mirror burden minus taxing-state burden, floored at zero, and confirm the workbook did not carry a negative into the total.
Confirm the retaliatory line is zero on every domiciliary-state tab.
Recompute total due = basic premium tax plus retaliatory excess and agree it to the amount remitted per the payment confirmation.
List every difference with its dollar amount and the component that caused it.
testing.done: the mirror burden, the floored excess and the total due are independently recomputed and agree to the workbook and the remittance within threshold.

testing.step: Test includable and excludable classification against the statute
actions: Read the retaliatory statute for each sampled state as it stood for the tax year, including any amendment effective mid-year.
Confirm every INCLUDABLE tag is supported by the statutory language and that ad valorem property taxes and special-purpose assessments were excluded.
Confirm classification is symmetric — the same component treated the same way on both sides of the comparison.
Treat any line carrying a tag with no quoted statutory basis as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every sampled classification is supported by tax-year statutory language and applied symmetrically on both sides.

testing.step: Recompute guaranty fund offsets, credits and carryforwards
actions: Trace each sampled assessment offset back to the assessment invoice and the cash payment in the GL.
Recompute the annual instalment under the state's recovery rule (commonly 20 percent per year for five years starting the year after payment) and check the carryforward roll-forward for expiries.
Confirm the offset sits on the side of the comparison the state's rule requires and was not double-counted in both the burden and the credit schedule.
Agree total credits claimed to the credit asset carried in the GL.
testing.done: every sampled offset traces to an invoice and payment, the instalment maths and carryforward reconcile, and no credit is double-counted.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise one tracker issue per exception with company, state, dollar variance, the component at fault and whether the tax was understated or overstated.
Assign a root cause from a fixed list: stale rate table, wrong domicile, asymmetric classification, basis error, credit misapplication, missing state.
Set an owner and a remediation date, and for understatements record the amend-or-true-up decision made by the Tax Director with its filing deadline.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and an amend-or-true-up decision.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the exception rate by state count and by dollar value and compare both to the stated thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — with the workpaper references that support it.
Have the Internal Auditor, who prepared and reviewed none of the sampled computations, sign the workpaper.
Report the result and any understatement above the escalation threshold to the Controller and the Audit Committee at the next sitting, and file the workpaper in the repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper with a stated conclusion, both exception rates and a committee reporting date is filed in the repository.
